verified_key_information_units.information: Gigasun reported revenue of SEK 239.7 million (up 9.8% YoY) and operating profit of SEK 73.5 million (up 21.1% YoY). Net profit was SEK -7.2 million, impacted by a SEK 3.8 million currency effect and SEK 3.5 million one-off cost; excluding these items, adjusted net profit was SEK 0.1 million. The full-year profit increase was significantly driven by a record Q3 with production up 36% and profit up 275% compared to Q3 2024.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Revenues amounted to SEK 239.7 (218.3) million... Operating profit amounted to SEK 73.5 (60.7) million... Profit after tax amounted to SEK -7.2 (-32.9) million and were impacted by a non-cash currency effect of SEK -3.8 (1.8) million as well as a one-off cost of SEK 3.5 million... The most notable development during the year was our record quarter in Q3. Production increased by 36 percent and profit rose by as much as 275 percent compared with the same period the previous year.

candidate_sentences.text: Group revenue increased 9.8% to SEK 239.7 million from SEK 218.3 million, while net revenue from electricity sales rose 9.9% to SEK 203.2 million.
Despite this increase, EBIT grew 21.1% to SEK 73.5 million, and the EBIT margin improved from 28% to 31%.
Results were also affected by a negative currency difference of SEK 3.8 million and a one-off cost of SEK 3.5 million.
Excluding these items, management reported profit of approximately SEK 0.1 million, compared with a loss of SEK 34.7 million in 2024.

verified_key_information_units.information: The company secured new financing of SEK 372 million through its Chinese subsidiary, extended loan amortization to 10 years at improved rates (3.60%), and postponed the SOLT4 bond repayment to November 8, 2026, enhancing liquidity and reducing financing costs.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: The company has entered into two agreements with the Chinese company Agricultural Bank Financial Leasing Co., Ltd to refinance approximately SEK 1,242 millions... The interest rate on the new financing is 3.60% and the amortization period has been extended from 7 to 10 years... The remaining bond, SOLT4, has been extended to November 8, 2026.

candidate_sentences.text: Financial expenses and similar items declined to SEK 82.0 million from SEK 88.7 million, reflecting the refinancing of Chinese debt.
Refinancing of approximately SEK 1.24 billion at 3.60% over ten years is underway and is expected to continue in 2026.

However, the SEK 70.4 million SOLT4 bond, carrying 14.25% interest, is due in November 2026, and management states that failure to secure additional financing would create significant uncertainty regarding continued operations.

details.completeness_justification: All key information units are adequately represented in the candidate summary. K3 is marked as PARTIALLY_PRESENT because while the refinancing and improved rates are mentioned, the specific details about the Chinese subsidiary and the exact amount of new financing (SEK 372 million) are not explicitly stated. However, the overall meaning of enhanced liquidity and reduced financing costs through refinancing is captured. All other criteria are PRESENT with core material meaning represented.

coherence_issues.description: Sentence S12 states that excluding certain items, management reported a profit of approximately SEK 0.1 million, but it does not clarify how this profit figure relates to the net loss reported in S9. The transition from a net loss to a marginal profit 'excluding these items' lacks explicit reconciliation details, creating a minor logical gap in the explanation of financial performance.

candidate_sentences.text: Excluding these items, management reported profit of approximately SEK 0.1 million, compared with a loss of SEK 34.7 million in 2024.

details.coherence_justification: The candidate summary is generally coherent with a clear progression of financial results and supporting factors. Most statements logically follow from one another, with consistent terminology and logical relationships between revenue, costs, and profitability metrics. The primary issue is a minor logical gap in S12 where the exclusion of specific items to arrive at a profit figure isn't explicitly tied back to the net loss reported earlier. There are no self-contradictions, organizational issues, or significant repetitions. The arithmetic differences between segment and consolidated figures are not claimed to be directly additive, so they do not constitute contradictions under the evaluation constraints.
